text: The Recluse reveals she knows the incantation that seals the Night Lord and is familiar with the ancient people buried in the crypt, having watched over them long ago since she does not experience mortality.
The Duchess, called back from her foster home, becomes the priestess of the Round Table Hold, described as a navigator even though the ship (the Hold) does not move.

The Duchess, as priestess, is rooted to the Round Table Hold and must share its fate; unlike other Nightfarers who escape as wisps of grace after the Night Lord falls, she is fated to cease existing along with the Hold.
When asked about the 'formless master' she serves, the Duchess replies that the seekers of redemption must on the third night band together and prepare to claim the life of the Night Lord.
The Wylder and the Executor share a relationship that is neither pure friendship nor rivalry, shaped by their different histories with institutional authority.
The Duchess and the Recluse have a dynamic contrasting inherited authority with earned, empirically-grounded knowledge.
The Night Farers' cooperative dynamics suggest each character's traits are completed or balanced by another's, such as the Wylder's pragmatism being sharpened by the Executor's judgment.
The Night Farers did not choose to come to Limveld; they were compelled by an irresistible calling that they could not decline or fully explain.
The Wylder is a warrior who served many causes and suffered repeated disappointments discovering those causes were unworthy, leaving them skilled but disillusioned.
In Limveld, the Wylder finds not a cause to believe in but a context where their combat competence has immediate value through survival and protecting companions.

The Duchess comes from an ancient lineage of the Golden Order's civilization, and markings on her weapons place her heritage at a point in Golden Order history predating the events of the base Elden Ring game.
It is unresolved whether the Duchess is literally ancient or whether her lineage has been preserved across time through some unexplained means.

The Guardian entered Limveld burdened by guilt after failing to protect his people, the Pinion Folk entrusted to him, becoming purposeless until arriving at the Round Table, where his heavy armor functions as a physical form of penance.

The Recluse was a scholar expelled from a sorceress institution connected to the Lands Between after conducting forbidden research into cosmological instability and worlds adjacent to the Lands Between.
The Recluse had theorized about Limveld's existence before arriving there, making her presence in the world a direct confirmation of her prior research.
The Ironeye has endured enough hardship that impermanence has become something navigated rather than merely survived, producing a calm that is not quite peace.
The Ironeye's calm stems from having released a relationship, community, or belief that once defined them, a loss hinted at through item descriptions.

The Raider came from a close-knit, egalitarian community valuing collective strength, a community type marginalized under the Golden Order's hierarchies, which was later destroyed while the Raider survived.
The Raider's fighting style reflects ingrained habits of fighting alongside others, even when fighting alone, due to years shaped by collective combat.
The Executor built their identity entirely around serving as the instrument of another authority's judgment, but has come to realize that some of the judgments they carried out were not righteous.
The Revenant died and returned, but is uncertain whether their returned self retains full continuity with who they were before death.
The Finger Readers appear in Limveld still practicing their interpretive function despite the apparent absence of the Two Fingers, the beings whose gestures they are meant to interpret.
Melina appears in Limveld with knowledge of the Night Lords and the three-night cycle that implies a familiarity beyond a single encounter.

The most compelling interpretation is that Melina has an ongoing relationship with Limveld, returning to it repeatedly in a cycle paralleling the three-night expedition structure, rather than visiting only once.
The game does not clarify whether Melina's presence in Limveld is directed by the Greater Will, by something that was once the Greater Will, or by her own choice.
The Keeper, who manages the hub between expeditions, is theorized to have originally been a Night Farer who came to Limveld, experienced the three nights, and chose or was unable to leave.
By staying in Limveld, the Keeper became something distinct from both an ordinary Night Farer and a true native of the world.
Wylder is characterized as finding enough immediate meaning in each task to keep going.
Duchess is characterized as carrying the weight of a tradition that still provides orientation even without the institution that produced it.
Guardian is characterized as trying again at a past failure with the determination that only genuine failure can produce.
Recluse is characterized as applying her understanding to a world that is itself the object of that understanding.
Ironeye is characterized as bringing acceptance and peace to a world that needs people able to work within impermanence.
Raider is characterized as bringing habits of community to a context that needs community to function.
Executor is characterized as discovering their own identity when no longer defined by service.
Revenant is characterized as continuing despite uncertainty about their own continuity, because continuation is what they have.
The Nightfarers' attendant at the Round Table is called the Iron Menial, a word meaning servant.
The Iron Menial resembles the marionette soldiers created by the Academy of Raya Lucaria in Elden Ring.
Wilder is a title (from Old English for 'wild animal'), not a proper name, and he hails from Wind Whale Null.
Wilder came to fight the Night Lord because the Night came to his home and massacred his tribe.
Wilder dreams of two horses galloping at Wind Whale Null, hinting at a sibling connection.
Wilder sustains injuries en route to the Round Table and, according to the Iron Menial and Revenant, will die from them after the Night Lord is defeated.
Wilder is seen eating pita bread taught to him by his mother, which the Duchess recognizes, evoking a 'wistful reminder of childhood.'
Wilder and the Duchess are implied to be twins, based on references to twin horses, the Duchess being adopted, and NPC dialogue confirming their familial relation.
The Revenant challenges the Duchess to a duel to test her resolve about continuing to fight the Night Lord despite her personal conflict.
The Raider tells the Duchess about his former navigator Weather Vain, who left the crew after a falling out and was never seen again, advising the Duchess to keep her cool.
The Duchess's plan is to have the Iron Menial, bonded via the Blessed Coin, protect Wilder after the Night Lord is defeated, accepting that she herself will disappear.
Wilder finds a note in the Duchess's belongings suggesting that a 'new knight' might break her link to the Round Table, and seeks the Recluse's advice.
The Guardian is a member of the Pinion Folk, a tribe of bird-like demihumans from the Winged Realm.
Conversations at the Round Table suggest the Raider may have been involved in the attack on the Pinion Folk, though his exact role is unclear.
The Guardian became a student of the Recluse at the Round Table.
The Guardian refuses a helmet made for him by the Raider because he vowed to never wear one again after failing to protect his flock.
A mysterious merchant visits the Round Table, gifts charms to the Nightfarers, and causes the Guardian to collapse upon receiving his.
The Guardian confronts and kills the merchant, discovering a ledger revealing the merchant supplied ancient animals to a demon connected to the cursed blades.
The Recluse accepts responsibility for creating the weapons that maimed the Guardian's people and awaits his judgment without excuse.
The Guardian spares the Recluse regardless of player choice, either laying down his weapon or destroying the Harmonious Brooch instead.
The Iron Eye originates from a group of master assassins called the Fellowship.
The Iron Eye receives orders from his custodian Isolde Day, the head of the Fellowship in the lands between, instructing him to await further orders.
Isolde Day later sends the Iron Eye a note ordering him to root out and retire a traitor connected to the destruction of a boarding house in Dusken Valley.
The Priestess reveals to Iron Eye that the traitor he seeks is another version of himself, a 'Condemned' Nightfarer who failed and succumbed to the Night.
After defeating a corrupted Iron Eye (the Night Huntsman), the real traitor leaves a note warning that he will come when the Night Lord nears.
The Duchess stops the real traitor from causing harm but does not kill him, allowing Iron Eye the chance to do so himself.
The traitor and the Fellowship, including Iron Eye, are 'those who live in death,' beings connected to the rune of death from Elden Ring lore.
Before his death, the traitor reveals to Iron Eye that the Fellowship members are already dead but cursed to never rest until the Night Lord is defeated.

Isolde Day sought a way to prevent the Fellowship's Scions (like Iron Eye) from being disposed of once their purpose was fulfilled, by keeping the war against the Night eternal so they would always have purpose.
The Raider is a pirate from the coastal waters who came to the lands between seeking to challenge the Night Lord for honor and glory.
The Iron Menial notices the Raider's love of battle and shows him a stone that summons fireworks, triggering an arena challenge requiring him to fight three opponents.
The Raider is revealed to be the Black Claw, while his final arena opponent, corrupted by the Night, is the White Horn, who also appears as an Ulcerated Tree Spirit during the fight.
The Raider's journal reveals that he and White Horn exchanged a necklace and helmet as tokens before their planned rematch, which never occurred until White Horn was taken by the Night.
A shop owned by a small jar creature in Limveld sells a Bismerch frame, which allows the player to find and duel a ghost at the Round Table, revealing it to be the Revenant.
The Revenant initially shows disdain for the other Nightfarers, believing the Round Table reeks of failure, and is challenged by the Guardian to prove herself by slaying a Night Lord.
The Revenant is revealed to be a doll, evidenced by jointed fingers and a crack on her cheek, and her flashbacks take place at the Northern Croft Manor.
In the flashback, an unidentified man kills a woman and then a young girl named Kloe, who was hiding; the girl's soul resides in a doll named Daphne.
The Revenant is the doll Daphne, who awakened with Kloe's soul or spirit shortly before Kloe's death.
The Revenant's final journal entry states she was never human and that 'the mantle of doll no longer fits her' after Kloe's death.
It is unconfirmed whether the Night Lord caused the massacre at Northern Croft Manor, as the killer is never explicitly shown to be the Night itself.
The only named figure associated with Northern Croft Manor is Edgar Northerncraft, an elderly bearded patron, who does not match the younger, beardless assailant seen in the flashback.
The Revenant possesses a spell tied to the Golden Order, suggesting a possible connection to nobility from Leyndell.
The Revenant also wields Death Lightning, a spell historically used by Godwyn during the war against the ancient dragons.
Helen wears the Page's attire, a noble outfit seen following perfumers in both Nightreign and Elden Ring.
Frederick is likely a Mad Pumpkin, an enemy type in both games whose lore describes them as former gladiators, fitting Leyndell's coliseum.
Sebastian is a large skeleton summon, similar to those called by the Tibia Mariner or found at grave sites like the Mountaintops of the Giants.
The Revenant's visual codex labels Helen as a page, Frederick as a cook, and Sebastian as a butler, implying her household held high noble status.
During the Revenant's ultimate attack, a skull is briefly visible behind her face, implying her puppet body may be built from actual human bones.
The Recluse originates from a place called the Deep Woods, where she searched for a being described as coiled in shadow, her lost infant.
The Menial doubts the Recluse's loyalty, fearing she may be planning something against the Round Table's cause.
The Menial asks the Recluse to slay Night-tainted enemies, specifically a Night-swallowed Golden Hippo, to prove her allegiance.
The Recluse recognizes the Night Shard as a means to reconnect with her lost infant child, believed to still be somewhere in the region.
After receiving the Night Shard, the Menial apologizes for doubting the Recluse and vows to help her search more earnestly.
The Vestige of Night once bore an engraving that is no longer legible, though the Menial seemed to know of its existence before seeing it, raising suspicion.
The Recluse senses the magic of her sister, the Witch of the Wheel, within the Vestige of Night.
The Night Lord is revealed to have resurrected the Witch of the Wheel, who the Recluse believed had died.
The Witch of the Wheel warns the Recluse to abandon her pursuit of the Night Lord, asking if she could truly slay her own child.
The Menial recalls dreaming that the Night Lord personally gave him the bone relic, as if wanting him and the Recluse to find it.
The Recluse ultimately resolves to confront the Night Lord in order to atone for her past actions.
The Executor is a silent character often found painting or observing a painting of the Erdtree, and keeps poetic journal entries.
The Executor hails from the Land of Reeds, a war-torn, isolated region briefly referenced in Elden Ring that is home to a samurai warrior caste.
Given his skill with a katana, the Executor is likely a former samurai from the Land of Reeds.
After defeating a guardian called the Executor's Cry, a cutscene reveals a dead Crucible Knight, a dead woman, and a second Crucible Knight who stabs himself with a katana.

Chapter 4 of the journal contains the line 'I am a guest, or perhaps an executioner,' followed by 'I will wait until your tree is complete,' implying the Crucible Knight delayed killing the painter until her work was finished.
Chapter 5 reveals the painting remains unfinished, so the painter sketches an old, silent friend from the Land of Reeds and entrusts the sketch to her guest.
The journal warns that another executioner will arrive before the painting is complete.
The Executor's description notes his armor is fused into his body and that he vanished after being imprisoned in the Lands Between, implying he survived his apparent suicide.
Chapter 7 of the Executor's journal states he has 'two faces in a soul drenched in blood,' hinting at guilt over past killings.
After Gladius's defeat, the Priestess reveals that the true Night Lord still lives and that more Night Lord traces must be found.
